title: COVID can wake up a slew of dormant viruses inside you
excerpt: Reactivation of typically harmless anelloviruses, in particular, seems to be linked with developing long COVID, study finds.
content_html:
A severe bout of COVID-19 can wake up an army of dormant viruses hiding inside the body.

That’s according to a study of more than 1,000 people hospitalized with the disease that is published today in Nature1. The analysis finds that this reactivation of pathogens is linked to especially intense bouts of COVID-19 and to the development of long COVID.

If further research reveals that reactivated viruses can cause people to become seriously ill, it could open the door to new treatments for COVID-19 and even long COVID, says Esther Melamed, a physician-scientist who studies neuroimmunology at the University of Texas at Austin and is a co-author of the analysis.

Although the study didn’t dive into how COVID-19 prompts viruses to reawaken, Melamed says that the disease “probably induces the stress that triggers the reactivations, and then these reactivations further amplify the inflammation” caused by COVID-19. In these cases, she adds, “COVID is not really acting on its own.”

The viruses inside

Nearly everyone is infected by a variety of viruses throughout their childhood and adolescence. A handful of these pathogens are never fully cleared from the body. Instead, they hide quietly inside cells for a lifetime, kept in check by a healthy immune system.

Four lessons COVID taught us about the immune system

Researchers have seen hints that these bystander viruses are reactivated in people with long COVID. So Melamed and her colleagues studied the situation systematically, collecting blood, nasal swabs and lung fluids from individuals hospitalized with COVID-19 in 2020 and early 2021. Nearly half of the participants experienced a reactivation of common viruses lurking in their bodies, the researchers found.

These pathogens included herpesviruses such as cytomegalovirus and Epstein–Barr virus, which causes glandular fever (mononucleosis), as well as anelloviruses, which are typically harmless and don’t cause symptoms. More than 90% of the global adult population has been infected with at least one of these pathogens2.

The team found that these viruses do not reawaken all at once after a person contracts the coronavirus SARS-CoV-2, which causes COVID-19. Instead, different viral families reactivate on their own timelines. Epstein–Barr virus and anelloviruses tend to surge early during a bout of COVID-19, peaking shortly after hospital admission. By contrast, cytomegaloviruses and herpes simplex viruses emerge around three weeks later, mainly in the respiratory system.

Could long COVID be linked to herpes viruses? Early data offer a hint

The “most striking” result is that this reactivation happens even in people with otherwise healthy immune systems, says Resia Pretorius, a physiologist at Stellenbosch University in South Africa. Some scientists had thought that a reawakening of viruses could happen only in people with a weakened immune system, such as those with HIV. But this study “overturns” that assumption, she adds.

Some people included in the study were receiving immunosuppressive drugs during their hospital stay for various conditions. However, this didn’t make them any more likely to experience virus awakenings than those who were not taking such medication. This suggests that the stress of a coronavirus infection alone can overload the immune system.

content_html_zh:
严重的 COVID-19 疫情可能会唤醒隐藏在体内的大量休眠病毒。

这是根据今天发表在《自然》杂志上的一项对 1,000 多名因这种疾病住院的人进行的研究得出的结果。 分析发现，病原体的重新激活与 COVID-19 的特别强烈的发作以及长期 COVID 的发展有关。

德克萨斯大学奥斯汀分校研究神经免疫学的医师兼科学家、该分析的合著者埃丝特·梅拉梅德 (Esther Melamed) 表示，如果进一步的研究表明重新激活的病毒会导致人们患上重病，那么它可能会为治疗 COVID-19 甚至长期感染的新疗法打开大门。

尽管该研究没有深入探讨 COVID-19 如何促使病毒重新唤醒，但 Melamed 表示，这种疾病“可能会引发触发病毒重新激活的压力，然后这些重新激活会进一步放大由 COVID-19 引起的炎症”。 她补充道，在这些情况下，“新冠病毒并不会真正自行发挥作用。”

里面的病毒

几乎每个人在童年和青春期都会感染多种病毒。 其中一些病原体永远无法从体内完全清除。 相反，它们一生都安静地隐藏在细胞内，并受到健康的免疫系统的控制。

新冠疫情给我们带来了关于免疫系统的四堂课

研究人员发现有迹象表明，这些旁观者病毒在长期感染新冠病毒的人体内重新激活。 因此，Melamed 和她的同事系统地研究了这一情况，从 2020 年和 2021 年初住院的 COVID-19 患者身上收集了血液、鼻拭子和肺液。 研究人员发现，近一半的参与者体内潜伏的常见病毒重新激活。

这些病原体包括巨细胞病毒和爱泼斯坦-巴尔病毒等疱疹病毒，它们会引起腺热（单核细胞增多症），以及指环病毒，它们通常是无害的，不会引起症状。 全球 90% 以上的成年人至少感染过其中一种病原体2。

研究小组发现，当一个人感染导致 COVID-19 的冠状病毒 SARS-CoV-2 后，这些病毒不会立即全部重新唤醒。 相反，不同的病毒家族会按照自己的时间表重新激活。 Epstein-Barr 病毒和指环病毒往往会在 COVID-19 爆发初期激增，并在入院后不久达到峰值。 相比之下，巨细胞病毒和单纯疱疹病毒在三周左右出现，主要出现在呼吸系统中。

长期新冠病毒可能与疱疹病毒有关吗？ 早期数据提供了线索

南非斯泰伦博斯大学的生理学家 Resia Pretorius 表示，“最引人注目”的结果是，即使免疫系统健康的人也会出现这种重新激活。 一些科学家认为，病毒的重新唤醒只会发生在免疫系统较弱的人身上，例如艾滋病毒感染者。 但她补充说，这项研究“推翻”了这一假设。

该研究中的一些人因各种原因在住院期间接受了免疫抑制药物。 然而，这并没有使他们比那些没有服用此类药物的人更有可能经历病毒觉醒。 这表明，仅冠状病毒感染的压力就会使免疫系统超负荷。
